One immense PRIVATE ROYAL BEDCHAMBER, not a throne hall. NORTH: a raised platform with a luxurious burgundy Persian-textile BED, reached by one broad step. A level main floor runs 12 meters SOUTH from that platform to the NORTH stairs of a roughly six-meter-square sunken seating area. Exactly THREE broad shallow steps descend SOUTH into this lower square. The lower floor has thick carpets and perimeter cushions with clear standing/walking space; a narrow exposed stone strip borders the central carpet. Massive columns, bronze objects and cabinets surround the MAIN floor. EAST/WEST entrances near the NORTH bed zone connect to dark corridors. All real companions may move on the main floor and rim, never down onto ANY recess step or lower floor. Only Zahhak and named dream/prophecy bodies occupy the lower square. No extra people.

PLAN 12 | LIGHT AND EXPOSURE

DEEP NIGHT. Blackness is the dominant image, not a blue-lit room. The ONLY source is one fixed vertical cold silver-blue shaft through a small ceiling opening directly above the CENTER OF THE SUNKEN SQUARE. It lands on one isolated circular patch of the LOWER floor. Its edge is sharply contained; faint airborne dust describes the shaft only inside it. Surrounding air remains black and clear, without room-filling haze. The beam never follows a person or changes position with the camera.

The lit carpet is a receiving surface, never an emissive floor: dark textiles absorb light, allowing only extremely weak localized bounce outside the patch. Do not brighten the set merely to explain the geography.

At close range, reveal a fragment at a time: one visible eye through a rigid mask opening, a narrow mask plane, a knuckle, a cloth fold or one moving snake glint. Never evenly expose the whole face or body. A turn can take that fragment back into black. Highlights belong to fixed world-space light, not the lens; no permanent eye catchlight, luminous eyes or light that tracks a face. Keep masks and skin unchanged. Emotional action stays legible through these fragments, movement and breath.

Expose for the lit patch without clipping it; lock exposure and black level through every cut and focus change. Close-ups and reverse angles receive no compensating light. Preserve large areas of true black without shadow recovery or a uniform blue wash; only sparse highlights carry restrained silver-blue color. Dream and prophecy figures never reveal identifying facial planes, mask details or eyes, including in low angles. Their silhouettes come from the existing shaft or lit floor behind them, never a new backlight. No aura, energy effects or glowing outlines.

Character and location references control identity and construction, not their photographed brightness. The written lighting overrides any brighter reference. Each shot's LIGHTING instruction defines the visible fragment; everything else may remain black. 35mm intimate from SOUTH of Zahhak. His gaze breaks from the empty EAST pool and turns NORTH; shoulders follow after the staff. Camera catches the delayed torso rotation, clips the mask and finds his eye again. His breathing changes from panic to exhausted determination without becoming calm.

40mm over his SOUTHWEST shoulder looking NORTH. Rack focus from near mask edge to the distant elevated royal bed beyond the NORTH stairs and long main floor. Burgundy bedding is only barely legible in weak moon-bounce; no spotlight or exposure lift reveals it. Shake persists while focus settles. This is the exact sleeping bed, no throne chair.

24mm close WEST-side profile, moving NORTH beside him from lower west margin to NORTH stair foot. 35mm low from WEST of the stairs looking EAST: NORTH/uphill is screen-left. Staff tip plants on tread one, stronger leg pushes and weaker leg follows. Camera rises unevenly with his hand. His body moves UP/left; never depict descent or a conveyor-like glide.

LIGHTING: Faint inward-edge bounce defines the supporting hand and first tread, not the whole stair. The body above that small fragment merges into black. Add no step light or upward-moving fill with the camera.

SHOT 12-05 | 11–13s | THE SECOND RISE

28mm tight WEST profile following his chest as he forces himself onto tread two. His free palm braces along the stair side. The high bed remains a dim distant shape NORTH/left, not suddenly close. A brief focus slip lands on the stone before recovering his trembling wrist.

SHOT 12-06 | 13–15s | THE LAST ATTEMPT

50mm from SOUTHWEST below his eye height as he faces NORTH/up. His gaze stays fixed beyond the top edge toward the bed. He draws a breath that will not fill and begins the final shallow step. Camera presses toward the mask, then recoils when his shoulders drop unexpectedly.

LIGHTING: Only a small eye or mask-edge fragment carries his last effort. His raised face does not acquire overhead light outside the shaft. Keep the upper landing and bed black except for the faint established trace.

24mm tight from WEST beside the stair, one continuous handheld take. Trying to clear the third step, his support knee fails; his free hand slides from the upper lip and his torso folds sideways across the broad lower treads. Camera drops late with him, briefly loses focus in cloth, then finds his collapsed shoulder and mask near the stair foot. This is a short heavy collapse, no long tumbling fall. Staff clatters within reach; snakes remain alive. His gaze no longer tracks and body goes limp. Hold close for the final breath, CUT TO BLACK at 20 seconds. Do not cut to helpers or recovery.

LIGHTING: The dropping camera finds only intermittent hand, shoulder and mask-edge fragments in weak stair bounce. Snakes move in darkness with occasional scale traces. Hold that same exposure through collapse and final breath; cut to black without relighting.

Zahhak lies unconscious-looking across the broad lower treads/foot of NORTH stairs; royal bed remains far above and beyond him. Staff fallen at his established side, mask intact, snakes living. Seven companions still on upper floor; none descends or reaches him before the cut. End immediately in black with no rescue scene.

Labored breath, repeated staff contacts, cloth scraping the rim, two imperfect upward footfalls, hand slipping, one body landing and staff clatter. No bone crack or stylized crash. Cut to silence with black; no closing music.
